job.text: Does your job ever involve building armor stands? Be honest.
How many of the Overseer's work orders are currently in your name?
Is your trade one the Overseer remembers, or one it forgets?
Have you ever been asked to smooth a wall that was already smooth?
Would your work have helped back at Quakefocus, during the throne years?
What does your job look like from the Overseer's side of things?
Do you ever carry a mug while you work, just in case?
Has a strange mood ever borrowed your workshop?
Which part of your work does {fort} take for granted?
How do you say no to a work order? Asking for a friend.
Do you work near any trees? Our readers are concerned.
If the liaison asked for your work at 210%, could you deliver?

mood.text: How are you holding up, compared to the dwarves of Searabbeys?
Has the mist ring by the pumps done anything for your spirits?
Are you happier this {season} than last?
Do you feel safe in {fort}? We mean safe, not 'Safety'.
Has the Overseer's latest decision helped or hurt your mood?
When did you last have a drink you actually wanted?
Is your mood the kind that demands rough gems?
How do you feel when the world blinks and starts again?
Has any of the furniture started to look like a target?
How are your spirits after all this goblin talk?
Does the windmill cheer you up, or just make noise?
How is your mood, in thrones? We use a scale of one to 148.

complaint.text: What would you remove from the work order list, if you could?
Should someone take a look at the garbage pit procedure?
How do you feel about the empty seats in the militia?
Who should be mayor, given that nobody wants to be?
Have you ever been charged with a production order violation?
Is there anything you'd like to throw down the garbage pit?
Should the 'Safety' burrow be renamed? To what?
What would you tell the Overseer about drinking water?
Has the liaison promised you anything that never came?
How many hospitals in {fort} have an actual doctor?
Which job has been sitting in the queue longest, in your view?
Are there too many armor stands in your life, or just enough?

deity.text: Do you pray for drinks, or for the sense to fetch them?
Has your god ever helped you out of a tree?
Which god watches over the dwarves of the old forts?
Do the gods see the Great Rewinds coming?
Would your god approve of the Overseer's work orders?
Does your god have a favorite throne? There are 148 to pick from.
Do you pray before going into the 'Safety' burrow?
Is there a god of empty militia seats?
What do you offer your god in {fort}? Rough gems are taken.
Do you think the gods were watching at Searabbeys?
Has your god ever answered in the form of a caravan?
Do you pray to be left off the smoothing roster?

kin.text: Does {kin} have strong views on the Overseer?
Has your {rel} ever had a strange mood?
Would {kin} make a good mayor? Somebody has to.
Is your {rel} the type who remembers to drink?
How did {kin} take the news about the garbage pit?
Does {kin} come from the old forts, or are they new?
What would {kin} say about you, if we asked? We may ask.
Has your {rel} ever joined the militia, even briefly?
Do you and {kin} keep away from trees together?
Does your {rel} ever write to the Herald? Be honest.
What has {kin} built that the fort should know about?
Is {kin} part of any running order you'd like to report?

nokin.text: Are any of your kin back at Searabbeys, or Quakefocus?
Do you count the cats as family?
Would you consider adopting an armor stand? We have spares.
Who checks that you've had a drink, if you have no family?
Is the militia captain a friend of yours? They need one.
Do you keep a seat for anyone at the tavern?
Would you marry if it got you a room above the garbage pit?
Has anyone in {fort} become like family to you?
Did you leave anyone behind when you came here?
Is the liaison your friend, or just someone who visits?
Do you prefer working alone, like our militia?
Who would you name as next of kin? The Herald needs a form.

last.text: Anything to say to the goblins at Searabbeys?
Any message for the dwarves who come after {fort}?
What would you tell a new migrant about this place?
If the world blinks tomorrow, what should we remember?
Any word for Iden Loloklolor, should the liaison be reading?
What do you want written on your slab? Briefly.
Should we print your advice on drinking in large type?
Anything for the militia captain, sitting off duty?
What would you like this {season} to finally fix?
Any message for the mayor's office, whoever is in it?
Last thoughts on thrones? We have to ask everyone.
What should the dwarves of {fort} do differently?

job_match.text: {level} {skill}, and the {prof} by title. At Quakefocus I'd have been buried in thrones. Here, only in work orders.
I am the {prof}, a {level} {skill}. The Overseer queued my job 400 times. I've done six. Proudly.
{level} {skill}. It says {prof} on the door and on the 300 orders pinned to it.
The {prof}, yes. {level} {skill}. I drink between every task. I learned that from the old forts.
I'm a {level} {skill}, and the {prof}. My trade has never once produced an armor stand. I check daily.
{prof}, {level} {skill}. I have never been near a tree, and my record shows it.
I am the {prof}. {level} {skill}. The mayor charged me with a production violation for doing it too well.
Proud {level} {skill}, sworn {prof}. Not a single throne in my portfolio. Well, two. Small ones.
{level} {skill}. The {prof} of this fort, and the only one who reads the order queue for fun.
I'm the {prof}. A {level} {skill}. If the world blinks, I start the same job again, without complaint. Mostly.
{level} {skill} and the {prof}. My grandfather did the same at Searabbeys, until the goblins moved in.
I am a {level} {skill}, the {prof}. Every job I finish, the Overseer adds two. It's a kind of compliment.
The {prof}. {level} {skill}. I keep a mug at my station. Nobody here dies of thirst on my watch.
{level} {skill}, the {prof}. The liaison once asked for my work at 210%. I gave a polite 100.
{prof} and {level} {skill}. I work in a fort with a mist ring. I have never been this damp or this happy.
{level} {skill}, sitting {prof}. I've filled more orders than the militia has filled seats, which is one.
The fort's {prof}. {level} {skill}. I have a little sign: 'Not Smoothing Today.' It is ignored.
{level} {skill}. They made me the {prof}, then gave me twelve hospitals' worth of other work.

job_mismatch.text: I'm the {prof} on paper. In practice, a {level} {skill}. The Overseer and I disagree, quietly.
{prof}, they say. {level} {skill}, I say. The order queue says 'build 1,981 armor stands'.
My title is {prof}. My hands are a {level} {skill}. My heart is mostly hauling.
The ledger says {prof}. I am a {level} {skill}. The ledger is also convinced we have a sheriff.
I was sent here as {prof}. I turned out to be a {level} {skill}. Migrants are like that.
{prof} by order of the Overseer. {level} {skill} by order of nobody. I prefer the second.
Technically {prof}. Actually a {level} {skill}. Theoretically in the militia. Nobody checks.
I hold the {prof} title, like the militia holds nine seats: in name only. I'm a {level} {skill}.
They wrote {prof}. I am a {level} {skill}. At Quakefocus, they'd have made me a throne carver.
I'm listed as {prof}. I've never done it. I'm a {level} {skill}, and I sleep fine.
The {prof}? Me? I'm a {level} {skill}. Someone is building a throne in my name somewhere.
Officially {prof}. My real trade: {level} {skill}. The mayor has filed a violation. I've framed it.
I'm down as {prof}. I'm a {level} {skill}. After the next Great Rewind I'll be listed as something else.
{prof}. That was a clerical error after the gods blinked. I'm really a {level} {skill}.
I am a {level} {skill} who has been labelled {prof}. Like the 'Safety' burrow, the label lies.
Called {prof}. Built like a {level} {skill}. Treated like a hauler. That's {prof} work for you.
The {prof}, apparently. I'm a {level} {skill}. Nobody asked, like nobody asked for 148 thrones.
I'm the {prof} the way the garbage pit is a garbage pit: on paper. I'm a {level} {skill}.

skill2_good.text: I'm a fine {skill2} as well. I could have saved Quakefocus a few thrones, but nobody asked.
I'm a good {skill2} too. I do it near the pumps, for the mist.
Also an excellent {skill2}. Better than the militia, which is one dwarf asleep.
Good at {skill2}, too. If the Overseer finds out, I'll get 900 orders for it.
I keep my {skill2} quiet. The last dwarf who was good at something got a work order the size of a hall.
My {skill2} is strong. I learned it from a dwarf who escaped Searabbeys.
I'm a solid {skill2}. The liaison praised it, then recommended an import agreement.
I'm very good at {skill2}. I'd teach it, but the fort is busy smoothing.
Expert {skill2} on the side. It's done every one of my strange moods proud.
Fine {skill2}, if I say so myself. The ghosts of Quakefocus have said nothing against it.
Talented {skill2}. Never once done it in a tree.
Strong {skill2}. The mayor tried to charge me for it, but it isn't on any order list.
Excellent {skill2}. Even the Great Rewinds couldn't take that away. They tried twice.

skill2_bad.text: I dabble in {skill2}. It went about as well as the 'Safety' burrow.
My {skill2} is weak. I'm trying, like the militia captain, alone.
I'm a poor {skill2}. The work came out like an armor stand: technically finished.
I am bad at {skill2}. The mayor filed a violation. For once I agreed with it.
My {skill2} is in progress, like 16,000 smoothing jobs.
Terrible at {skill2}. I'd rather haul garbage. Actually, no, I would not. Not anymore.
I'm learning {skill2}. Slowly. Like the Overseer learning to put out drinks.
Bad {skill2}. I tried it once during a mood and the workshop asked me to leave.
My {skill2} is about as good as the fort's sheriff, who doesn't exist.
{skill2}? A bit. Mostly I make the sound of it.
I have tried {skill2}. The results went into the garbage pit, and I did not follow them. Lesson learned.
My {skill2} skills went missing after a Great Rewind, if they were ever there.
I'm a poor {skill2}. The liaison saw it and said, 'There is much to share,' then left.

mood_ecstatic.text: Wonderful! I walked through the mist ring three times today. My beard is soaked and my heart is full.
Ecstatic. I had a drink, then another, and I didn't die of thirst at all. A personal best.
I'm glowing. I counted the armor stands and the number went DOWN. Someone must have sold one.
Overjoyed! The Overseer cancelled one of my orders. Just one. I'll remember it forever.
Never better. I stood at the bottom of a tree and decided not to climb it. Growth.
Bliss. I saw the militia captain on duty. Briefly. Then off again. Still, I saw it.
I could sing. I have been singing. The liaison joined in and asked for an import agreement.
Thrilled! There is a mug in every room I've been in today. The old forts would weep.
Elated. I sat on one of the 148 thrones. It was very comfy. Now I understand Quakefocus.
Grand! The world blinked this morning, and I woke up in exactly the same good mood.
I am delighted, and it is not my fault. I've checked.
Radiant! I didn't go near the garbage pit once this week. My family is very proud.
Over the moon, which I have never seen, but the windmill people tell me it's nice.

mood_happy.text: Happy, thanks. I had a drink AND a meal on the same day. {fort} is getting fancy.
Pretty good. The pumps keep misting me. I've stopped asking why and started smiling.
Good! I haven't been charged with a production violation in a whole season.
Cheerful. My workshop is free and nobody in a mood has claimed it. Yet.
Happy enough. I'm nowhere near the 'Safety' burrow, and it shows in my face.
Fine and dandy. The Overseer gave me a job I actually know how to do.
Glad. I passed a goblin rumor in the hallway and it turned out to be just a cat.
Good, thank you. My bed is not an armor stand. Not everyone at Quakefocus could say that.
Content-plus. There's ale, there's stone, and nobody has asked me to smooth it.
Happy. I met the liaison and he only said 'There is much to share' twice.
Quite good. The windmills turn, the cistern is full, and my socks are mostly dry.
Happy. Every morning I check I'm not stuck in a tree. So far, so good.

mood_content.text: Fine. Like a fort that has drinks AND remembers they exist.
So-so. Not Searabbeys-bad. Not throne-room good.
Steady. Like the militia: always off duty, but at least it's there.
Middling. Like smoothing: one wall at a time, never finished.
All right. I've survived worse. I've read about worse, anyway, in the old Sentinel.
Average. The mist ring got me wet, and the sun dried me off. A wash.
Okay. The Overseer hasn't noticed me lately, which I count as a good sign.
Content. I've decided I don't need a throne. I've decided several times.
Even. No moods, no tantrums, no trees. A quiet sort of life.
Fine, thanks. Like a drink you didn't know you needed until you had it. Have it.
Neutral. The goblins are somewhere else. The gems are somewhere else. So am I, mentally.
Middle of the road, which in {fort} is a smoothed road, so very nice road.

mood_stressed.text: Stressed. Every time I hear 'work order', I see armor stands.
Edgy. I was told to go to the 'Safety' burrow for a drill. I said no.
Rattled. The mayor's office slipped a violation under my door. I don't even know what I made.
Tense. I was handed a rough gem request and every gem in the fort was cut.
Worried. I heard the stairs creak and thought: forgotten beast. It was a cat. Still.
Frayed. I've been gathering plants in the rain since breakfast. Breakfast was last week.
Not good. The militia captain asked me to join. I said I'd think. I'm still thinking. Hard.
On edge. The world blinked and I lost a whole afternoon of work.
Itchy and cross. The mist ring sprayed me during my nap. It's meant to cheer me up.
Strained. I've been hauling refuse. I keep looking behind me.
Twitchy. I saw a tree. Just one. That was enough.
Sore. I spent all day smoothing a wall nobody will ever walk past.

mood_very_stressed.text: Awful. I've been queued for 600 thrones and I'm not even a carpenter.
Rotten. I'm thirsty, and I can see the drinks from here. I know how this story ends.
Bad. I've been sent to the garbage pit three times. I came back twice. Wait. No, three.
Dire. The liaison wants rings at 210% and somehow it's my problem.
Miserable. I'm the only dwarf in my squad, and I'm not even in a squad.
Very bad. Somebody keeps throwing things into the pit while I'm still in it.
Grim. I want rough gems and there aren't any. I'm starting to understand the moods.
Horrible. I dreamed about Quakefocus. All 1,981 of them. They were standing.
Bleak. I'm not allowed in my workshop because a child is having a mood in it.
Terrible. The 'Safety' burrow is my assigned place. I've written my will twice.
Shattered. The Overseer has scheduled me to smooth the smoothed parts.
Very low. My drink is in a barrel I'm not allowed to touch. Storage policy.

mood_breaking.text: I am going to smash an armor stand. There are enough. Nobody will notice.
One more work order and I'm throwing the queue down the garbage pit. With me on top.
Get the militia. Oh wait. Get the militia CAPTAIN. Get them to wake up.
I'm about to go up a tree and refuse to come down. You know how that ends.
I'm on the edge. Ask me about drinks. Go on. Ask me.
I'll topple a throne. Then another. Then 146 more. I have the time.
I am breaking, and the mist ring is not helping. Turn it OFF.
Someone touch my workshop, I dare you. I have a rough-gem look in my eye.
I'm close to going berserk. The 'Safety' burrow would be a fine place for it.
I'll start a Great Rewind myself, with my bare hands.
Back off. I just found out the hospital has no doctor and I'm the patient.
I'm one 'There is much to share' away from biting the liaison.

deity.text: I pray to {deity}. Mostly for drinks to be put where I can reach them.
{deity}. I asked for fewer armor stands. {deity} is still thinking it over.
I follow {deity}. {deity} has never sent me to a 'Safety' burrow, which is more than I can say for some.
{deity}, always. When the world blinks, I'm sure it's {deity} rubbing an eye.
I trust {deity}. I trust the Overseer less. Please print it in that order.
{deity} kept me out of trees for three years. That's a miracle round here.
My god is {deity}. My grandmother prayed to {deity} at Searabbeys, all through the Meat Watch.
{deity}. I lit a candle when the goblins took Searabbeys. Still burning. Small candle, big grudge.
I pray to {deity} before every trip to the garbage pit. {deity} has a perfect record so far.
I follow {deity}. {deity} has nine empty seats in heaven, like our militia, and keeps them clean.
{deity}, who I like to think would have taken the mayor's job. Nobody else will.
I keep a shrine to {deity} next to the pumps. It's always a bit damp. {deity} doesn't mind.
{deity}. I asked {deity} for a rough gem during my mood. I got a cut one. Gods have a sense of humour.
I pray to {deity}, mostly about thrones. I don't need one. I'd just like to know why there are 148.
{deity} watched over Quakefocus too. {deity} must have seen a lot of armor stands.
I worship {deity}, quietly, in the tavern, between drinks. That's where {deity} lives, I'm sure.
{deity}. The liaison once asked if {deity} had an import agreement. I said no. He wrote it down.
I follow {deity}, who has never charged me with a production order violation.
{deity}. I asked for guidance about the Great Rewinds. {deity} said, 'Again?'

kin_alive.text: My {rel}, {kin}, reminds me to drink. Twice a day. I've never once been thirsty. Bless them.
{kin} is my {rel}. They keep me away from trees. I keep them away from the garbage pit.
{kin}? A darling. Won't go near the 'Safety' burrow. Smart, that one.
My {rel} {kin} has been queued for 200 thrones. I bring them snacks.
{kin} is doing well. They tried the militia once, and the captain was so glad they cried.
My {rel}, {kin}, has had two strange moods. Both wanted rough gems. Both got cut ones. Tense times.
{kin} is my {rel}, and we argue about whether the Overseer means well. I'm winning.
{kin}? Lovely. They walk through the mist ring on purpose. Odd, but happy.
My {rel} {kin} has a grudge against the liaison. 'There is much to share' my foot, they say.
{kin} is thriving. They've never once been charged by the mayor's office. Suspicious, honestly.
My {rel}, {kin}, keeps a list of every throne built at Quakefocus. All 148. With names.
{kin} is well. They stay near the drinks, as all our family does since Searabbeys.
{kin}, my {rel}, can smooth a wall in an hour. Sadly, the Overseer found out.
My {rel} {kin} survived a Great Rewind and now dates things as 'before' and 'after'.
{kin} is lovely. They think the windmills are talking to them. Maybe they are.
My {rel}, {kin}, keeps a mug tied to their belt. Family tradition, after the thirst years.
{kin} is great. They refuse to sit on armor stands, which is wise, as they aren't chairs.

kin_dead.text: My {rel}, {kin}, went down to the 'Safety' burrow. The Herald knows how that one went.
{kin} is gone. They had drinks nearby. They had so many drinks nearby.
{kin}, my {rel}, fell asleep in a tree and never came back down. I don't climb anymore.
My {rel} {kin} hauled garbage. I don't want to talk about the pit.
{kin} rests in the catacombs now. Nice spot. Quiet. Not a work order in sight.
{kin} passed during a mood. They wanted a rough gem. There wasn't one. I'm still cross.
My {rel}, {kin}, died at Quakefocus, beside a pile of gems. Not one of them would have saved them.
{kin} is gone, but they built three thrones first. I sit on one every year.
I lost {kin} to the goblins at Searabbeys. I still don't go north.
{kin}, my {rel}, rests below. I pour a drink by the slab, since they never got enough.
{kin} is gone now. They were in the militia. All of it, at the time.
My {rel} {kin} went in the forgotten beast attack. The stairs have not been forgiven.
{kin} is gone. They were waiting for the loom room. I still wait for it, for them.
{kin} passed. Their ghost visited once, asked if the armor stands were finished, then left.
My {rel}, {kin}, rests in peace. Their slab is smooth. The Overseer made sure. Three times.

nokin.text: No family. I came over from the Quakefocus diaspora. We don't do family. We do grudges.
Nobody. Just me and the mist ring. The mist ring does call me 'dear', or seems to.
No kin here. My family stayed at Searabbeys. The goblins live there now. I don't write.
Alone. I have 1,981 armor stands, though, in spirit.
No one. I've thought of joining the militia just for company. It's one dwarf.
No family. I have a barrel I like. I visit it daily, so no thirst for me.
Just me. I tell the windmills my secrets. They keep turning, so they must agree.
Nobody. I'm the mayor's favourite person to charge, if that counts as a relationship.
No kin. The liaison calls me 'friend'. He calls the wagon that, too.
No one. The world blinked and when it reopened I was still single.
Nobody special. I have a seat by the cistern that nobody takes. That's close.
No family. Our fort keeps losing dwarves to trees. I keep my distance from everyone, and trees.
Single. I'm saving myself for whoever takes the mayor job. Could be a long wait.
No kin. I talk to a ghost from the old fort. It mostly asks for drinks.
Nobody. I'm married to my station, which the Overseer has cancelled and requeued twice.
Alone. I'm a militia of one, emotionally speaking.
No family. I do have a throne. A small one. I won it in a card game at Quakefocus.

signoff.text: Drink something. Right now. I'll wait.
Remember Searabbeys: 1,994 drinks, and still. Drink yours.
If the Overseer orders an armor stand, ask how many. Then sit down.
Stay out of trees. That's it. That's the whole advice.
'Safety' is a word, not a promise.
Never haul garbage while somebody is still throwing it.
Cut gems are pretty. Rough gems are mood insurance. Keep a few.
Somebody please be mayor. Anybody. You, reading this. Yes, you.
The militia has nine empty seats and one tired captain. Go say hello.
When the world blinks, check your mug is still there.
There is much to share, as the liaison says. Mostly paperwork.
Two hospitals and no doctor is not a medical plan. Tell your friends.
Count your thrones, {fort}. Then stop counting. It's healthier.
Walk through the mist ring once a day. Doctor's orders. We have no doctor.
Smooth one wall, enjoy it, and leave the other 15,999 for another day.
The stairs go both ways. So do forgotten beasts.
Look after your children. They have moods now, apparently.
Keep a spare loom room. A weaver will thank you.
The goblins have Searabbeys. Let them keep the Meat Watch.
Strike the earth, then drink. Mostly drink.
A mug on the belt beats a barrel in the stockpile. Ask Searabbeys.
Quakefocus had 148 thrones and nowhere to sit. Don't be Quakefocus.
The Herald loves you, {fort}. Please stay hydrated.
Mind the garbage pit, and the garbage pit will mostly mind you.
Every work order is a suggestion. Some are 1,981 suggestions.
Say hello to the windmills. They're doing their best.
If the mayor charges you, plead 'Overseer'. It works every time.
Watch the stairs this {season}. Something always comes up.
Ask the dwarf next to you if they've had a drink. Then ask again.
Don't sit on the armor stands. They're not for that. Nothing is.
The goblins of The Destined Wickedness can wait. Dinner can't.
Don't trust a tree. Don't trust a burrow labelled 'Safety'. Do trust the Herald.
Seven silk scraps is not a cloth supply. Learn from Quakefocus.
The Amusing Duties has had 48 owners. Your socks need only one.
Long live Oddom Oltartilesh, and long live the drinking schedule.
Fill the cistern, fill the mugs, fill the militia. In that order.
The world has blinked before. It will blink again. Keep your boots on.
Smooth floors, full barrels, empty trees.
If a mood asks for rough gems, ask the jeweler first. Nicely. Quickly.
Hello to the dwarves of the old forts, wherever their ghosts are tonight.
Gather plants if you must, but not across the whole map in the rain.
Champion, hammerer, sheriff: all open. Apply today. Please.
Stay above the 'Safety' line. Thirty levels above it, ideally.
Don't wait for the loom room. Learn to weave standing up.
Hydrate, migrate, don't speculate.
{fort} forever, or at least until the next fort.
Visit the catacombs, but come back. That's the important part.
Never accept rings at 210%. Counter at 105%.
Remember Claspedserpent. Not for any reason. It's just a good mace.
If you see the militia captain on duty, write to the Herald. We'll print it big.
Make one throne, if you must. Then stop. Then really stop.
Keep the drinks where the miners are, and the miners where the drinks are.
Your Overseer is doing their best. We assume. We have not checked.
Be kind to elves visiting. Be kinder to the barrels.
Happy {season}, and happy hauling, and happy not-being-in-the-pit.
Next time the forgotten beast comes up the stairs, go up the other stairs.
Pray to whoever you like, but drink to everyone.
Watch out for the Crazed Hex. And for carp. Mostly carp.
Signing off, before the Overseer finds me and gives me a work order.
Good night, {fort}. Leave a mug by your bed.

decks.text: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was mid-'{job}' when the Herald arrived. We checked: not an armor stand. We relaxed.
The Herald interrupted {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) in the middle of '{job}', one of several thousand queued orders.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, agreed to talk during '{job}' on one condition: that we bring a drink. We brought two.
Our reporter found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, busy with '{job}', at a safe distance from any tree.
{dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) took a break from '{job}' to speak, which the mayor's office may log as a violation.
While the Overseer added three more jobs to the queue, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, finished '{job}' and spoke to us.
Mid-'{job}', {dwarf}, {age}, the fort's {prof}, gave the Herald the time between one work order and the next.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was doing '{job}' by the mist ring. Our notebook did not survive. These are from memory.
The Herald met {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, mid-'{job}', and nowhere near the 'Safety' burrow, as is wise.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, kept at '{job}' throughout the interview. Our reporter was asked to hold a mug.
Sent to do '{job}', {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) did it, which in {fort} is news on its own.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, spoke with the Herald during '{job}', and checked twice that we were not a work order.
Busy with '{job}', {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) still found time to air a grudge or two. We printed both.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, did '{job}' under the windmills while our reporter took notes and got dizzy.
Found mid-'{job}': {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, who asked us not to mention thrones. We mention them below.
The Herald visited {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, at work on '{job}'. The militia captain was off duty, as usual.
{dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) answered our questions in the middle of '{job}' and made sure to drink between each one.
Halfway through '{job}', {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, told us the Overseer would 'want to read this.' Hi.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was assigned '{job}' this {season}, and the Herald was assigned {dwarf}.
Our correspondent waited until {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) finished '{job}'. Then another '{job}' came up.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, took questions during '{job}'. A liaison walked past and said there was much to share.
On '{job}' duty, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, spoke to the Herald about life, drink, and armor stands.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, kept one eye on '{job}' and the other on the stairs. Old habits from the beast days.
We spoke to {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) during '{job}'. The garbage pit was mentioned once. Then never again.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was busy with '{job}' and with a rough gem in the pocket, just in case of a mood.
The Herald caught {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, on '{job}' duty, the fourth job this hour by our count.
{dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) stopped '{job}' just long enough to say hello, and to ask if we'd seen the mayor.
Interrupting '{job}' in {fort}, the Herald found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, calm and well-watered.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was busy with '{job}' when we visited. Not smoothing. We checked twice.
Between '{job}' and the next order, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had just enough time for the Herald and a drink.

idle_decks.text: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had no job at all, a rare event the Overseer has been asked to stop correcting.
The Herald found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, idle by the pumps, being gently misted, and asked a few questions.
With no work order in sight, {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) spoke freely. The Overseer will fix that soon.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was idle, which in {fort} is either a holiday or a clerical error.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, doing nothing near the tavern, mug in hand. A dwarf of wisdom.
{dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) was between jobs and between thrones. We took the chance to chat.
Idle and unashamed, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, gave the Herald a full afternoon. The armor stands can wait.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was sitting off duty, much like the militia, and agreed to talk.
No job, no mood, no tree: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was found safe and idle in the meeting hall.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had been idle since the world last blinked, and was glad of company.
Our reporter found {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) waiting for a job that was stuck behind 16,000 others.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had nothing to do this {season} and spent it telling the Herald all about it.
Taking a well-earned rest, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, met the Herald by the cistern, mug full.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was idle and asked us not to tell the Overseer. Sorry. The Overseer reads this.
We met {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, idle beside a stack of armor stands nobody remembers ordering.
Found without a task, {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) offered the Herald a seat on a spare throne.

decks.text: {nick} has now raised {topic} with the Herald {n} times. The Overseer has queued a response. It is behind 1,981 armor stands.
On day {days} of the {topic} matter, {nick} asked the mayor's office for help. The mayor's office charged {nick} with a violation.
{nick} first raised {topic} on {since}. The world has blinked since then. {topic} did not.
Interview {n} on {topic}. {nick} reports no progress, but has had a drink, which the Herald considers a win.
{nick} would like {topic} added to the Overseer's work orders. We regret to say it already is, several hundred times.
{nick} says {topic} is 'like the Safety burrow: sounds fine, isn't.' The Herald has printed this {n} times now.
The {topic} saga entered day {days}. {nick} has started a petition. One signature. Like the militia.
{nick} raised {topic} with the liaison, who said there was much to share and recommended an import agreement.
Since {since}, {nick} has held firm on {topic}. Quakefocus held firm on thrones for a while too. Consider the record.
{nick} returns on {topic}, visit number {n}. The Herald's archivist has asked for a hospital. One with a doctor.
{nick} told us {topic} is now 'the 148 thrones of problems.' We do not know what this means. We print it anyway.
Day {days} of {topic}. {nick} has been seen near a tree, thinking. Readers are asked to bring {nick} down gently.
{nick} wants it known that {topic} would not have happened at Searabbeys. We checked. It would have.
{nick} has asked the militia to look into {topic}. The militia, being one dwarf off duty, has not.
Readers following {topic} since {since} will know {nick} is not giving up. Nor is the issue. They have become close.
{nick}'s grievance over {topic} reached interview number {n} today, and the garbage pit has been asked to stay out of it.
Asked about {topic} for time number {n}, {nick} sighed, took a drink, and said, 'Same.' A full transcript follows.
Day {days}: {nick} still says {topic}. Our reporter still writes it down. The Overseer still smooths a wall nearby.
{nick} has filed {topic} with every vacant office: mayor, sheriff, hammerer and chief medical dwarf. No reply yet.
The {topic} matter, opened on {since}, has now outlived three work orders and one strange mood.
{nick} says the gods have noticed {topic}. The gods are said to have blinked. Twice. Nothing changed.
Talk number {n} with {nick} on {topic}. {nick} asked us to pass the matter to the Overseer. Overseer, consider it passed.
{nick} reports that {topic} is still unresolved, and offered to show us. We were taken down 30 levels. We left.
{nick} would like the Herald to treat {topic} as front page news. This is page {n}. It's a start.
After {days} days of {topic}, {nick} has started calling it 'my armor stand.' The Herald does not ask why.
{nick} brought {topic} to the tavern, the depot, and the mist ring. Only the mist ring listened, and it just sprayed.
{nick} insists {topic} is a fort issue, not a personal one. The Herald has opened a file under both, just in case.
Interview {n}: {nick} on {topic}, again. Even the ghosts of Quakefocus are said to be following along.
{nick} kept the {topic} grudge alive through {days} days and one Great Rewind. A record, the Herald believes.
The {topic} story continues. {nick} asks that the Herald stop calling it a saga. Day {days} of the saga continues.
